title: Research
text:
Three research fronts, one method: turn satellite
imagery and climate series into information that can be checked against official
data. Each front has an explorer, the numbers behind it and what still does not
work.


  
    01
    
      Research front
      Agriculture
    
  
  Crop classification and vegetation index series at
  plot scale. Our own base covers 359,600 plots across 897 municipalities in five
  states, with data from 2020 to 2025.

  
    Vegetation index series
    17 indices, 23 dates per year and 499,720 series per plot,
    11.5 million rows in total. Switch the layer to see the same data from another
    angle.

    
      
        
        
        
      
      
        Seasonality by state
        NDVI heatmap
        Cloud filter
      
      Average seasonality of the vegetation indices in the five states, by satellite overpass date.
    

    
      
        
        From raw series to ready series: original observation, interpolation and smoothing.
      
      
        
        Valid observations per plot after the cloud filter.
      
    
  

  
    Season start against the official window
    We detect the start of the season from satellite and compare
    it with the ZARC planting window in Campo Verde, Mato Grosso. The official
    window describes soybean well and barely covers the rest of the farm
    calendar.

    
      
        Soybean
        
        65.5%
      
      
        Cotton
        
        7.6%
      
      
        Second crop maize
        
        3.3%
      
    
    Share of plots whose detected season start falls inside the official window, in Campo Verde, Mato Grosso. Soybean accounts for 2,971 of 4,539 plots. In the other municipalities analysed, soybean ranges from 72.7% to 84.5%.
  

  
    359,596Plots mapped
    897Municipalities
    17Vegetation indices
    11.5MSeries rows
  

  
    
    
      Project 01Crop classification by plotSoybean, maize and cotton identified plot by plot and season by season. Against INPE field data in Campo Verde, mean accuracy was 98.7% for soybean, 91.5% for maize and 90.0% for cotton. The public reference scores 99.3%, 82.4% and 64.4%.
      Project 02Our own plot level baseA base generated every season, reprocessed every cycle and extensible to new states: 359,600 plots across 897 municipalities in Bahia, Maranhão, Mato Grosso, Tocantins and Paraná.
      Project 03Time series of indices17 indices, 23 dates per year and 499,720 series, with a documented cloud filter and interpolation, 11.5 million rows in total.
      Project 04Grouping by behaviourEach plot and season holds 1,670 values across indices, daily series and climate series. Grouping by similarity reveals behaviour profiles inside a portfolio.
      Project 05Productivity and riskOne of the groups, with 1,240 plots, shows productivity 18% below average, sandy soils and 3.1 times more claim occurrence. The group is classified as high risk.
    
    
  



  
    02
    
      Research front
      Forests
    
  
  Forest segmentation at property scale, validated
  against official data from INPE. The model reaches 0.85 IoU in quarters that
  were not part of training.

  
    The same scene, six years later
    
      
      
      
      
      2020 Q1
      2026 Q2
    
    Model prediction for the same scene, in 2020 Q1 and 2026 Q2. Drag the divider to compare.
  

  
    Six years of forest, quarter by quarter
    26 quarterly maps, from 2020 Q1 to 2026 Q2, walked through
    with a slider.

    
      
        
        2026 Q2
      
      
        
        2026 Q2
      
    
    Forest prediction by quarter. Images load on demand, one quarter at a time.
  

  
    What the model sees and how confident it is
    
      
        
        
        
      
      
        Model prediction
        Registry areas
        2023 reference
      
      Model prediction for the 2023 Q3 quarter, covering the full analysis area.
    

    
      
      Model confidence pixel by pixel, in six classes, in the 2023 Q3 quarter. Each colour shows how stable that pixel decision is.
    

    
      Where the model fails. Validated against DETER alerts and
      PRODES polygons, recall for the forest class sits at 0.28 and 0.26, and the
      predicted area is larger than the alerted area, 165.3 km² against 27.1 km²
      from DETER and 44.5 km² from PRODES. Part of that is a difference of
      criteria: the official alert marks recent clearing, the model marks absence
      of canopy. We publish the number because it defines the correct use of the
      product.
    
  

  
    Results by quarter and by cell
    
      
        
        Performance by quarter in the temporal context experiment, which uses the previous quarter as extra information.
      
      
        
        Performance by cell of the scene, showing where the model is more or less stable inside the same area.
      
      
        
        Confusion matrix of the quarterly model. The near infrared band takes IoU from 0.72 to 0.74.
      
      
        
        Area per year according to the model and according to the two official systems, DETER and PRODES.
      
    
  

  
    0.85IoU in the best model
    26Quarters mapped
    180GeoTIFF delivered
    203DETER alerts assessed
  

  
    
    
      Project 01Satellite forest segmentationA SegFormer model with Sentinel-2 imagery from the Brazil Data Cube: 0.74 IoU in the quarterly version with the near infrared band and 0.85 with temporal context. The analysis grid is 9,712 by 11,110 pixels, at about 10 metres per pixel.
      Project 02Spatial generalisationTrained in one region and tested in another, to measure what the model learns about forest and what it learns about place: 0.79 from west to east and 0.76 from south to north.
      Project 03Forest inside registry areasEvaluation with the rural property as the unit: 0.797 IoU. Forest covers 24% of the registry area, against 37% of the bounding box around the scene.
      Project 04Validation against DETER and PRODES203 DETER alerts and 9,105 PRODES polygons compared with the prediction, with the limits published alongside the result.
      Project 05Quarterly deliveries180 GeoTIFF files delivered, one per quarter and per extent, from 2020 to 2026, ready for use in a geographic information system.
    
    
  



  
    03
    
      Research front
      Climate
    
  
  Climate trends and agricultural risk in 15-year
  windows, municipality by municipality, linking the climate series to crop
  behaviour.

  
    15 years of climate in Nova Mutum, Mato Grosso
    Six trend indicators between 2011 and 2025, compared with the
    1985 to 2010 average where a reference series exists.

    
      
        Maximum temperature
        0
        increase over 15 years, about 0.076 °C per year
      
      
        Mean temperature
        0
        increase over 15 years, about 0.066 °C per year
      
      
        Minimum temperature
        0
        increase over 15 years, about 0.056 °C per year
      
      
        Warm nights
        0
        nights with minimum above 22 °C, 7.7 more nights per year
      
      
        Annual rainfall
        1,631 mm
        period average, 7.7% below the 1,767 mm of 1985 to 2010
      
      
        Dry days in the rainy season
        24.5 days
        period average, 5.3 days more than the 19.2 days of 1985 to 2010
      
    
  

  
    Operational risk and systemic risk
    The reading is always relative to the neighbourhood, to
    separate what is a farm problem from what is a regional problem.

    
      
        Operational risk
        Management, pest, condition and grower context
        What sets one plot apart from its close neighbours, under the same climate and the same soil.
      
      
        Systemic risk
        Drought, frost and regional dry spells
        What hits the whole region, and therefore cannot be solved by an isolated management decision.
      
    
  

  
    15Years of series
    6Trend indicators
    +108Warm nights
    2011 to 2025Period analysed
  

  
    
    
      Project 01Municipal climate trend15-year windows with six indicators per municipality, to separate trend from year to year variation.
      Project 02Warm nights and heat stressMinimum temperature above 22 °C accumulated 108 extra nights in 15 years. It is the indicator that talks most directly to yield loss.
      Project 03Rainfall and dry spellsAccumulated rainfall and dry days in the rainy season, compared with the 1985 to 2010 reference.
      Project 04Vegetation indices as a drought sensorThe crop response to water shortage shows up in the index series before it shows up in productivity, which links this front to Agriculture.

title: Finding the underlying viscoelastic constitutive equation via universal differential equations and differentiable physics
text:
Authors: Elias C. Rodrigues, Roney L. Thompson, Dário A. B. Oliveira, Roberto F. Ausas
Published: November 2025, Engineering Applications of Artificial Intelligence, v. 160, 111788 (Pergamon)
Read the article




Determining the appropriate constitutive model to describe the behavior of a given material is a fundamental, yet challenging, aspect of rheology. While data-driven methods present a promising path for refining these models, a more in-depth investigation into the capabilities and limitations of emerging techniques is required. This research addresses this gap by employing Universal Differential Equations (UDEs) and differentiable physics to model viscoelastic fluids, merging conventional differential equations with neural networks to reconstruct missing terms in constitutive models. This study focuses on analyzing four viscoelastic models, Upper Convected Maxwell (UCM), Johnson, Segalman, Giesekus, and Exponential Phan, Thien, Tanner (ePTT) using synthetic datasets. The methodology was tested across different experimental conditions, including oscillatory and startup flows. Relative error analyses revealed that the UDEs framework maintains low and stable errors (below 0.3%) for the UCM, Johnson, Segalman, and Giesekus models under various conditions, while exhibiting higher but consistent errors (4%) for the ePTT model due to its strong nonlinearity. These findings highlight the potential of UDEs in fluid mechanics while also identifying critical areas for methodological improvement. Additionally, a model distillation approach was employed to extract simplified models from complex ones, emphasizing the versatility and robustness of UDEs in rheological modeling.




Fig. 4. Avaliação da extrapolação dos modelos UDE para a tensão de cisalhamento \((\sigma_{12}^*, t^*)\) com entrada \(\dot{\gamma}^*(t^*) = 3\cos(1.5\,t^*)\). Os pontos destacados em verde correspondem aos pontos de treinamento, \(t^* \in [0, 20]\). A curva azul ilustra a solução numérica da equação diferencial, chamada de solução de referência (“ground truth”). A curva preta representa o modelo UDE antes do treinamento, enquanto a curva vermelha ilustra o modelo UDE após o treinamento. Os seguintes parâmetros foram utilizados: \(\xi = 0.4\) (Johnson, Segalman), \(\alpha = 0.2\) (Giesekus) e \((\xi, \epsilon) = (0, 0.4)\) para (ePTT).

title: Deep Clustering for Climate: Analyzing Teleconnections through Learned Categorical States
text:
Authors: Lívia Meinhardt, Dário Oliveira
Published: April 2026, arXiv preprint arXiv:2604.22909
Read the article




Understanding and representing complex climate variability is essential for both scientific analysis and predictive modeling. However, identifying meaningful climate regimes from raw variables is challenging, as they exhibit high noise and nonlinear dependencies. In this work, we explore the use of Masked Siamese Networks to discretize climate time series into semantically rich clusters. Focusing on daily minimum and maximum temperature, we show that the resulting representations: (i) yield clusters that reflect meaningful climate states under our modeling assumptions, offering a simplified representation for downstream use; (ii) enable sampling and analysis of specific climate scenarios; and (iii) exhibit statistical associations with El Niño events, underscoring their scientific relevance. Our findings highlight the potential of self-supervised discretization as a tool for climate data analysis and open avenues for incorporating richer climate indicators in future work.




Extensão espacial da região de estudo selecionada (Cerrado brasileiro) utilizada para o treinamento e a avaliação do modelo.





Análise de probabilidade com defasagem que demonstra a sensibilidade dos regimes aprendidos em defasagens \(\tau \in \left[ −12, +12 \right]\) meses em relação ao Índice Niño Oceânico. Defasagens negativas indicam comportamento precursor antes do El Niño, enquanto defasagens positivas indicam respostas postergadas após o pico do ENOS.

title: About Us
text:
GAIA Lab develops
machine learning methods that turn satellite imagery and
climate data into verifiable information about forests,
agriculture and climate. Created in
2024 at FGV EMAp, the lab works at territorial scale, across five Brazilian
states, and checks every result against official references.


  0Researchers
  0Research fronts
  0Publications
  0Founded




  
    2024
    The lab is created at FGV EMAp, in Rio de Janeiro, bringing together machine learning research applied to Earth observation.
  
  
    2025
    Build of our own plot level base and of the vegetation index series: 359,600 plots across 897 municipalities in five states, covering 2020 to 2025.
  
  
    2025
    Team at the 14th International Conference on Climate Informatics, in April, and the first forest segmentation models with Sentinel-2 imagery from the Brazil Data Cube.
  
  
    2026
    Forest product at scale, with 26 quarterly maps delivered from 2020 to 2026 and validation against INPE's DETER alerts and PRODES polygons.
  





  
    
    
    
  
  
    
    






    
    
  





  
  
    Principle 01Reproducible scienceThe same run, repeated, varies by up to ±0.0076 IoU. Every result comes with that margin stated.
    Principle 02Validation against official referencesEach product is compared with DETER, PRODES, ZARC, MapBiomas and the Rural Environmental Registry.
    Principle 03Territorial scale359,600 plots, 897 municipalities and five states, with series from 2020 to 2025.
    Principle 04Transparency about limitsWe publish where the model fails. Validated against DETER alerts, recall for the forest class is 0.28.

title: Exploring EnMAP hyperspectral images and ensemble deep learning for classifying forest land-cover types in Brazil
text:
Authors: Matheus Pinheiro Ferreira, Matheus Santos Fuza, José M. S. M. Viveiros, Tomás Ferranti, Dário Oliveira, Giulio Brossi Santoro, Paulo Guilherme Molin, Catherine Torres de Almeida, Angélica F. Resende, Danilo R. A. de Almeida, Yelu Zeng, Ricardo Ribeiro Rodrigues, Pedro H. S. Brancalion
Published: April 2026, International Journal of Remote Sensing, v. 47, n. 7, p. 3213-3238 (Taylor & Francis)
Read the article




Spatially explicit information on forest land-cover types is critical foreffectively managing and conserving forest ecosystems and mon-itoring restoration initiatives. This study delves into the potential ofthe Environmental Mapping and Analysis Program (EnMAP) hyper-spectral satellite for distinguishing between tropical forest land-cover types in São Paulo, Brazil. We developed and evaluateda novel ensemble deep learning approach, integrating a 1DConvolutional Neural Network (CNN), an autoencoder, anda Recurrent Neural Network (RNN), for pixel-wise classification. Wealso assessed the impact of spectral resolution by comparingEnMAP data with simulated Landsat 8 and Sentinel-2A data, andinvestigated the influence of band selection on classification accu-racy. The study focused on mapping forest land-cover types, includ-ing conserved remnants, natural regeneration, restorationplantations, and monocultures. Our findings reveal significant dis-tinctions in spectral responses across these forest land-cover types.The ensemble deep learning model significantly outperformedindividual deep learning models and traditional Support VectorMachine (SVM) classifiers, achieving the highest weighted F1-Score of 0.700. EnMAP data further achieved significantly higher F1-scores than Sentinel-2A and Landsat-8 (p < 0.05), with the greatestgains observed for natural regeneration and restoration planta-tions. Interestingly, band selection did not universally improveclassification performance for the deep learning models, and insome cases, led to a decrease in accuracy. While monocultureswere classified with high accuracy, misclassifications were observedbetween natural regeneration and restoration plantations, andbetween conserved remnants and natural regeneration, reflecting their spectral similarities. This study provides valuable insights intothe effective use of space-borne hyperspectral imagery and ensem-ble deep learning for robust forest land-cover type mapping intropical regions, emphasizing the critical role of high spectral resolution.




Localização da área de estudo no estado de São Paulo, Brasil. São apresentadas composições em cores reais de dezesseis cenas do satélite hiperespectral EnMAP abrangendo o estado de São Paulo. Um detalhe no canto inferior esquerdo destaca a distribuição espacial das parcelas de campo estabelecidas em quatro tipos de cobertura florestal.





Abordagem de ensemble baseada em aprendizado profundo. title: Exploring EnMAP hyperspectral images and ensemble deep learning for classifying forest land-cover types in Brazil
text:
Spatially explicit information on forest land-cover types is critical foreffectively managing and conserving forest ecosystems and mon-itoring restoration initiatives. This study delves into the potential ofthe Environmental Mapping and Analysis Program (EnMAP) hyper-spectral satellite for distinguishing between tropical forest land-cover types in São Paulo, Brazil. We developed and evaluateda novel ensemble deep learning approach, integrating a 1DConvolutional Neural Network (CNN), an autoencoder, anda Recurrent Neural Network (RNN), for pixel-wise classification. Wealso assessed the impact of spectral resolution by comparingEnMAP data with simulated Landsat 8 and Sentinel-2A data, andinvestigated the influence of band selection on classification accu-racy. The study focused on mapping forest land-cover types, includ-ing conserved remnants, natural regeneration, restorationplantations, and monocultures. Our findings reveal significant dis-tinctions in spectral responses across these forest land-cover types.The ensemble deep learning model significantly outperformedindividual deep learning models and traditional Support VectorMachine (SVM) classifiers, achieving the highest weighted F1-Score of 0.700. EnMAP data further achieved significantly higher F1-scores than Sentinel-2A and Landsat-8 (p < 0.05), with the greatestgains observed for natural regeneration and restoration planta-tions. Interestingly, band selection did not universally improveclassification performance for the deep learning models, and insome cases, led to a decrease in accuracy. While monocultureswere classified with high accuracy, misclassifications were observedbetween natural regeneration and restoration plantations, andbetween conserved remnants and natural regeneration, reflecting their spectral similarities. This study provides valuable insights intothe effective use of space-borne hyperspectral imagery and ensem-ble deep learning for robust forest land-cover type mapping intropical regions, emphasizing the critical role of high spectral resolution.

Cada modelo gerou saídas de probabilidade de classe, as quais foram posteriormente combinadas utilizando um mecanismo de votação rígida (hard voting) para gerar a previsão final do ensemble.
